successors.name: Roman Republic
successors.text: the kingdom after Gentius's defeat at Scodra in 168, which the Romans divided into three administrative divisions called merides (Gentius page): the Labeates and the district of Acruvium, Rhizon and…

rulers.name: Pinnes (under the regencies of Teuta and Demetrius of Pharos)
rulers.title: King, a child; regents Teuta (231-228) and then Demetrius of Pharos

ledger.x: 256: the Ardiaean kingdom, the Illyrian kingdom of the Adriatic coast, stands at Scodra and Rhizon.

c. 247: the kingdom reaches north to Narona. 'His state stretched from Narona in Dalmatia south to the river Aoos and Korkyra' (Agron, who ruled 250-231); the page dates none of the annexations and 247 is Cliopatria's year for the shape that reaches Narona.

c. 239: the kingdom reaches the Epirote coast. The page has Agron annex part of Epirus and Epidamnus and garrison them (undated, within 250-231); 239 is Cliopatria's year. The same page dates the Epirote change: "In 234 BC, the royal succession in Epirus came to an end, and a federal republic was instituted."

c. 230: Phoenice returned. The page has Phoenice returned under a truce and the Illyrians withdraw, undated; the cells near 40 N, 20 E that Cliopatria's 230 shape no longer holds are read as this return.
228: the First Illyrian War ends in a treaty; Rome "established a protectorate over these Greek towns" (Epidamnos, Apollonia, Corcyra, Pharos) and took the Parthini and Atintani as clients.
196: Pleuratus III is 'rewarded by the Romans in 196 BC, with lands annexed by the Macedonians'.
180: 'In 180 BC, during his early reign, the Dalmatae and Daorsi declared themselves independent.'

wars.name: Medion campaign against the Aetolians
wars.outcome: Agron's Illyrians defeated the Aetolians at Medion; Agron died in the winter of 231, within a few days of the Aetolian victory (Agron page).

wars.name: First Illyrian War
wars.outcome: Rome landed in 229, took the Greek towns and the Parthini and Atintani under protection and, by the treaty of winter 229/228, cut the Illyrians off south of Lissus and the Drin; the core north of the Drin stayed with Teuta.

wars.name: Third Illyrian War
wars.outcome: Gentius, who had gone over to Perseus in 169, was defeated at Scodra by L.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; the extent is Agron's 'from Narona ... south to the river Aoos and Korkyra'.
The one line the pages name is the treaty limit of 228 at Lissus and the mouth of the Drin; north of it the borders are soft.
